title: akit manifest
description: What a machine or a repository subscribes to: the global manifest in your platform's config directory, or the .akit.yaml beside a repository's .git. The schema describes the shape of one file and nothing beyond it: whether a source exists, whether a kit is in it, whether a pin resolves and whether two subscriptions render to one name are questions akit answers, not questions a validator can.

version.description: The manifest format. One version exists; a file naming another is refused rather than read optimistically.

harnesses.description: Who gets rendered for. Absent means [detected], which is every harness found on this machine. `detected` is a name like any other in the list, so naming one more harness does not turn the rest off.

skills.description: Skills, as a mapping of source key to the kits wanted from it. A mapping rather than a list, because two skills cannot contradict each other and their order is therefore noise.

rules.description: Rules, as a list of single-source entries. The one kind with an order: two rules can contradict each other, and the order they are listed in is what decides which wins.

agents.description: Agent definitions, as a mapping of source key to the kits wanted from it.

block.description: One kind's subscriptions, keyed by source. A key names a git repository in any of the forms `akit help sources` lists, and may carry a `#<commit>` pin.

kits.description: What is wanted from one source: a kit name, a kit that needs more than its name, a list of either, or "*" for every kit of this kind the source holds.

name.description: A kit as its source calls it, or "*" for every kit of this kind.

renamed.description: A kit installed under a different name, which is what two sources shipping one name is solved with.

as.description: What this kit is called once it is on disk. It goes onto the rendered directory and into the copied SKILL.md header.

harness.description: One harness, as a bare name taking its default destinations, or as a mapping naming a destination for a kind it reads from more than one place.

doors.description: Which destination one harness takes each kind through. A kind left out takes that adapter's default, which is what a bare name has always meant. Which destination names a harness offers is the adapter's answer: `akit list` names them.
